_register: Address the reader formally (usted) but avoid the pronoun: use the impersonal infinitive for buttons, menu entries and steps ("Escanear el código", "Renovar"), and the third-person usted imperative only where a sentence needs it ("Pulse Intro para registrar la devolución"); no exclamation marks, no tuteo (no "tú" forms, no voseo).
_quotes: Spanish angular quotes « » for quoted titles and names (e.g. «{{title}}»); nested quotes use “ ”; the arrow → stays.

copy.note: One physical copy of a book with its own barcode; this is the standard school-library term in Spain. Plural: ejemplares.

record.note: Catalogue entry of a title (ficha bibliográfica / registro). Use "ficha" for short labels; "registro" is more technical and clashes with "registrar" (to register a return).

patron.note: Spanish libraries say "usuario" (lector is less formal). Use the masculine generic in labels ("Usuarios"); never "cliente" or "socio".

card.note: Library card: "carné de biblioteca" in Spain; "carnet" is a variant spelling, use "carné". In Latin America "credencial" or "tarjeta" are also heard; "carné" is understood everywhere. Plural: carnés.

overdue.note: "Préstamos con retraso" for the list, "{{days}} días de retraso" for the count. Avoid "vencido" (sounds like expired) and "moroso" (implies fines, which the program never has).

reminder.note: The printed slip asking for the return; "reclamación" is stronger and is used in Spain for the formal step, but "aviso" fits a school better. Short form: "aviso".

call number.note: Standard term in Spain ("signatura topográfica"). In Latin America "número de clasificación" or "clasificación topográfica" is also used; "signatura" is understood by librarians everywhere.

spine band.note: In Spain "tejuelo" is the label on the spine carrying the signatura. If a descriptive form is needed: "banda del lomo" (lomo = spine).

label.note: Adhesive label with a barcode: "etiqueta de código de barras" when it must be specific.

class.note: A school class such as 3 B is "grupo" or "clase" in Spain and "curso" in Latin America. Use "clase" for the class patrons belong to; "curso" means the school year/grade (e.g. 3.º ESO), so keep it for the level only.

group.note: Used for a group of teachers and for the class group of the database; do not use "grupo" for the school class label alone (use "clase").

classification.note: How fiction and non-fiction are sorted (CDU in Spain). Verb: clasificar.

stocktaking.note: Checking the shelves against the catalogue; in Spanish libraries this is "expurgo" only for weeding, so keep "inventario".

wish list.note: Established library term in Spain for the books users ask the library to buy. Alternative for plain wording: "lista de deseos".

census.note: Registering patrons with their photo; "censo fotográfico" also works.

class upgrade.note: Moving every class up a year at the end of the school year; also "promoción de curso". Here "curso" is the school year, not the class.

anonymise.note: Spelled with z in Spain and Latin America ("anonimizar", not "anonimitzar"). Erases the personal data for good.

staff account.note: A shared login per role. "Personal" here means staff, as in "personal de la biblioteca".

backup.note: Preferred in Spain over the anglicism "backup" or the Latin American "respaldo".

restore.note: Noun: restauración (f.). Putting a backup back.

language pack.note: A translation of the interface. "Idioma" is the term for a language in the interface (not "lengua").

colour set.note: A palette of the interface; "paleta de colores" is also fine and shorter.

scanner.note: The USB barcode reader that types like a keyboard. "Escáner" is a common short form; use "lector" in labels and "escanear" for the verb (to scan).

wizard.note: The first-start sequence of questions; "asistente de configuración" in full.

student.note: Use the masculine generic in labels ("Alumnos"). "Estudiante" is more usual in Latin America and is gender-neutral; "alumno" is the school term in Spain.

teacher.note: Use the masculine generic in labels ("Profesores"). "Docente" is gender-neutral and common in Latin America; in Spain "profesorado" is the collective.

school year.note: In Spain "curso escolar" (2026/27); "año escolar" is the Latin American usage.

template.note: Print templates for cards, labels and slips.

note.note: Notes for the desk and notes pages; "anotación" is more formal and longer.

return desk / circulation desk.note: The area label "Circulation desk" in the navigation; in Spain "mostrador de préstamo" or "punto de préstamo". The menu entry "Loans" stays "Préstamos" and "Returns" stays "Devoluciones".
